about: The 9869 streams as lines: the flowing water too small to be a river, worked out on the drainage the rivers and lakes were drawn from (DrainageDirection.png and DrainageFlow.png), and drawn as the rivers are. Made by Scripts/streams/t1_streams.py against vcom/Scenes/Map.tscn as it was then, whose rivers, lakes, borders and roads they meet, follow and keep clear of.
order: Largest first: id 1 carries the most water. A stream is listed after the stream it joins.

fields.ends_in: stream (it joins the stream whose id is in joins), river (it ends on the line of the river whose id is in joins, as the game's scene draws it), lake (it ends inside the lake whose id is in joins), sea, or dry (it runs out of water in dry country)
fields.from_lake: the lake of LakeMap.png it flows out of: every lake that touches no river and has water leaving it has its outlet drawn
fields.kingdom, kingdoms: the kingdom of KingdomMap.png most of it lies in, and all it touches
fields.largest_flow_m3s, flow_at_end_m3s: the most water it carries, and what it carries at its end
fields.points: [x, y] in pixels of the map (a whole number is the middle of a pixel), thinned where it runs straight and with a point wherever it bends, so that it nowhere turns more than 10 degrees at one point
fields.flow_m3s, width_px: the most water it has carried so far, and its width, at each point
fields.course: the middles of the cells of DrainageDirection.png its water runs through, as the drainage has it: the line it was drawn from

which_are_drawn: A stream begins where the ground it gathers (km2) times the water it carries (m3/s) reaches 5.32: what 20 km2 of the Deciduous Forest gives, so wet country begins its streams on less ground and dry on more (about 9 km2 in the Evergreen Rainforest, 18 in the Tundra, 105 in the Grassland), and only where it carries 0.2 m3/s or more. Once begun it runs on until it meets a river, a lake, the sea or a bigger stream; in the Desert and the Grassland, where water is lost to the ground, only while it carries 0.1 m3/s. The outlet of every lake that touches no river is drawn, down to what it reaches, if water leaves the lake. Nothing is drawn where only storms run: no dry washes. A stream that nothing joins is left out if it is under 1.5 km long.
width_rule: width_px = 0.7 + 0.396 * flow ** 0.36, a quarter more in swamp and tropical rainforest country (7 and 9 on TerrainMap.png), and never under 0.75 or over 1.95: under the narrowest river's 2 px
wandering: A stream's line is its course smoothed, then swung from side to side, in loops about a dozen widths long where its bed is nearly level (as the rivers are) and a little everywhere, never more than 0.3 of the way to other water; where it would still cross a bigger stream it is drawn with less, or ended where it meets it.
meeting_other_lines: A stream ends on the line of the river, or the stream, it joins, inside the lake it reaches, or 3 px past the land's edge, in the coast's line. Where it follows a border's line for 12 px or more it is put on that line, and along_borders gives the line of the border's colour the game's scene lays under it there. Where a road runs along it for 12 px or more it is moved off to the side, clear of the road.
along_borders_fields: Where a stream runs on a border's line: the border's rank, the scene's name for the border, the stream's id, the stream's width there, and the line: the border's own points from where the stream comes on to it to where it leaves.
